why: "delete the 19 decorative status dots; de-duplicate the 15 md:grid-cols-3 marketing rows".
The audit's own rule is the test: keep the dots that encode severity or state, delete the ones that
decorate a label that already says the same thing; equal three-card rows are acceptable for reference
indexes and banned for feature/marketing rows.
statusDots        - what survives the sweep, with the reason each one is data rather than ornament.
A dot is counted as `rounded-full` + a small square size + a `bg-<token>` colour.
equalThreeCardRows- every three-column row on the page surface, with what kind of content it holds.
`kind: "cards"` is a feature/card row: its signature must be unique across pages,
so the same three-across shape cannot be pasted onto a second marketing page.
Every entry is asserted against a live scan of frontend/src by __tests__/designSignature.test.js,
so a new decorative dot or a pasted card row fails the suite instead of shipping quietly.

2026-10-06: pages/UserDashboardPage.tsx loses its `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3` entry. The definition list it counted moved into components/user/PublicProfileCard.tsx, which both the dashboard preview and /u/<username> now render; the scan walks pages/ only, so a row in a component is out of scope rather than un-ledgered.

2026-10-08: components/district/DistrictBriefBody.tsx gains three kept dots. The Cupertino Precision sweep (51bd0ed) rounded the geospatial heatmap's legend swatches from `rounded-sm` to `rounded-full`, which puts them inside the dot rule; they are severity encoders next to a label each, so they are ledgered as kept rather than deleted. The sweep changed 62 frontend files and no ledger, which is why the backend job went red on the next push instead of on the sweep itself.
